title: Generalized Thermodynamics and Phase Transitions of Vaidya-adS Black Holes
summary: This work investigates the thermodynamics of non-stationary anti-de Sitter (adS) black holes and their gauge-gravity duals. To model a non-equilibrium process, we employ a time-dependent Vaidya-adS metric to describe the collapse of a null fluid and the subsequent thermalization of the dual field theory. We introduce an effective version of free energy as a quasilocal probe to be used in a dynamical setup. By analyzing how this quantity evolves, we show that a first-order phase transition occurs when the final black-hole mass exceeds the limit established by the Hawking-Page temperature. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the final state only approaches the thermal behavior of the N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory for mass states much larger than the adS radius. Finally, we compute the boundary energy-momentum tensor using holographic renormalization and compare the resulting energy density with the strong-coupling limit. This demonstrates that the dual description provides a consistent framework for both the equilibrium and non-equilibrium thermodynamics of strongly coupled gauge theories.

title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
comment: Submitted to A&A. 18 pages, 15 figures, 6 tables
summary: Galaxy morphology traces the physical processes that shape galaxy evolution, but non-parametric diagnostic boundaries depend on image quality and preprocessing. We investigate the classification of regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish (ram-pressure-stripping candidate) galaxies in the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Using galmex measurements of ten non-parametric morphological indices, we evaluate two-dimensional diagnostic planes with a cross-validated Bayesian kernel-density classifier and combine all indices using probability-calibrated LightGBM models. For separating regular spirals, regular ellipticals, and perturbed systems, the most informative planes combine Shannon entropy with $M_{20}$ or asymmetry indices, reaching balanced accuracies of 0.76-0.77. We provide survey-specific probabilistic boundaries in the entropy-$M_{20}$ and entropy-shape-asymmetry planes. Separating mergers from jellyfish candidates is more challenging; the best two-dimensional combinations, all involving concentration, reach balanced accuracies of approximately 0.73. The calibrated three-class LightGBM model achieves a balanced accuracy and macro-F1 score of 0.89, while the four-class model achieves 0.75 and 0.76, respectively. We provide class probabilities and preferred classifications for 1,744,454 galaxies. Our results show that non-parametric morphology identifies broad structural disturbance reliably, but distinguishing its physical origin is harder: jellyfish candidates occupy a relatively coherent region of parameter space, whereas mergers span diverse and overlapping morphologies.

title: Defects in Topological Symmetric Orbifolds and their String Dual
summary: We review defect topological field theories with finite gauge groups. We then concentrate on restriction and induction defects between symmetric orbifold theories and recall that the defects form an algebra. This requires identifying the features of restriction and induction defects that are independent of the order of the symmetric group, which is natural in a grand canonical framework. The construction leads to Khovanov's categorification of the Heisenberg algebra. The bulk algebra of partial permutations corresponds to the endomorphisms of the identity defect in the category. We also interpret the Hurwitz theory defects in the dual Gromov-Witten theory. This gives a defect descendant interpretation to higher level operators that arise in the integrable hierarchy of the Gromov-Witten theory of curves. In further applications, we relate known defects to our symmetric group theoretic description. For seamed surfaces, we determine the boundary operator algebra for higher values of the covering degree n and provide asymptotics for the large n growth of the number of boundary operators.

title: Prospects of Detecting Cosmological Domain Walls in the Cosmic Microwave Background
summary: Topological defects are a generic prediction of field theories with spontaneously broken symmetries, and domain walls, the two-dimensional defects left by a broken discrete symmetry, are among the simplest. We study the imprint of dark, purely gravitationally interacting domain walls on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), in the regime where a low symmetry-breaking scale $η$ allows the walls to evade the Zel'dovich overclosure bound while remaining cosmologically relevant. The relativistic repulsion of matter by a planar wall carves out an evacuated void bounded by an overdense shell, and we compute the resulting photon deflection field analytically for walls both aligned with and arbitrarily inclined to the line of sight. The deflection stamps coherent, strongly non-Gaussian distortions onto the temperature sky, with a characteristic two-peak structure set by the relativistic displacement scale and an inclination dependence that vanishes for face-on walls. Because these signatures are localised and anisotropic, they are poorly captured by two-point statistics; we therefore analyse them with a curvelet/wavelet decomposition matched to the wall's geometry, and with simulation-based inference, training a Neural Posterior Estimator (NPE) to recover the scattering redshift $z$, energy scale $η$, and inclination $θ$, and a Neural Ratio Estimator (NRE) to evaluate the likelihood-ratio test statistic for limit-setting. Casting these methods as sensitivity forecasts for a South Pole Telescope-like (SPT) survey, we find that the curvelet and wavelet statistical thresholds populate a common $η\sim 10-100$ MeV band over the accessible redshift range. The neural-ratio sensitivity curve, which exploits the full map morphology, reaches a factor 1.3-1.9 lower in $η$ at $z \gtrsim 20$, or $\sim 2-7$ in the wall tension, landing essentially on the per-resolution-element noise floor.

title: AMICO galaxy clusters in KiDS-1000: Cosmological constraints from the two-point correlation function
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: In this paper we study the clustering properties of an optically identified photometric galaxy cluster catalogue from KiDS-1000. The sample was identified by the AMICO algorithm and consists of 9049 clusters with $S/N\geq3.5$, in the redshift range $0.1\leq z<0.8$, spread over an effective area of 838.78 deg$^2$. Clusters are selected according to their observed intrinsic richness, with thresholds of $λ^*{obs}\geq 20,25,30$ within $0.10\leq z<0.30$, $0.30\leq z<0.45$ and $0.45\leq z<0.80$, respectively. We measure the multipoles of the two-point correlation function over different ranges of scales from 5 $h^{-1}$ Mpc to 150 $h^{-1}$ Mpc. We model the clustering signal in the context of the $Λ$CDM cosmology, accounting for the main observational effects, such RSDs and photo-$z$ uncertainties. The effective bias of the cluster sample is estimated via a mass-richness scaling relation. For the MCMC analysis, we adopt Gaussian priors on the parameters of the mass-richness scaling relation, and broad, uniform priors to derive cosmological constraints on the cold matter density parameter, the power spectrum amplitude and the structure growth parameter, $S_8\equivσ_8 \sqrt{Ω{m}/0.3}$. Specifically, we find $Ω_{m}=0.24^{+0.02}{-0.02}$ and $σ_8=0.86^{+0.13}{-0.10}$ representing an improvement in precision over both the 2D and 3D AMICO clustering analyses performed on the previous KiDS data release. Moreover, we obtain $S_8=0.77^{+0.10}_{-0.08}$ in $1σ$ agreement with the AMICO KiDS-1000 number counts constraints estimated from the same catalogue, as well as with some results from external early- and late-Universe data sets. Our work strengthens the potential of cluster clustering as a complementary and competitive probe, to be included and further developed with the final KiDS-Legacy data release, and in other future Stage-IV photometric redshift surveys.

title: Non-singlets and the phase diagram of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
summary: The quantum mechanics of one $N\times N$ Hermitian matrix in the infinite $N$ limit is well known to define a two-dimensional string theory when the quartic coupling constant $g$ is tuned to a special negative value $g_*$. We study the thermodynamics of this Matrix Quantum Mechanics (MQM), treating the SU$(N)$ symmetry as a global symmetry. Crucially, the non-singlets, i.e. states in non-trivial representations of SU$(N)$, implement the effects of vortices on the discretized worldsheets. This random lattice model has the low-temperature $c=1$ and high-temperature $c=0$ phases, with the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition separating them. We map out the phase diagram in the coupling--temperature plane, which is separated by the critical stability curve $T_c(g)$ extending from $g_*< g <0$. We study this curve using the non-perturbative matrix bootstrap and low- and high-temperature perturbation theory, which explain the thermal instability. At low temperatures, thermally excited non-singlets backreact on the Fermi sea of matrix eigenvalues, causing it to spill over. At high temperatures, the theory is described by an effective matrix integral obtained by dimensional reduction on the thermal circle; the eigenvalue distribution of the zero mode becomes unstable at the critical coupling. We conjecture that the BKT transition occurs at a special point on the critical curve and estimate its position. Finally, we switch to the regular square lattice and study the MQM-inspired Villain model, where the link factor is the one-dimensional propagator on a circle. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we map out the BKT transition in this model.

title: The Galactic Center Reference Frame: A 30-Year Solution
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Accepted by ApJ
summary: Stellar orbits probe the metric of and mass around the Sgr A* massive black hole. To enable study of the black hole, the surrounding mass, and tests of gravity, a precise reference frame must be established and maintained. We present an updated stellar maser-based reference frame for the inner parsec of the Galactic Center, referenced to the radio continuum of Sgr A*. This work synthesizes 30 years of astrometric observations of 15 SiO stellar masers and the Sgr A* continuum at 43 GHz. The uncertainty in the mean offset of the maser ensemble from Sgr A* is 0.08 mas in the current epoch and will decay to 0.10 mas by 2030. At a distance of 8.2 kpc, these correspond to position uncertainties of 0.6 AU and 0.8 AU, respectively, which is similar to or smaller than the stellar SiO-emitting region. The mean maser proper motion uncertainties are 0.05 mas yr$^{-1}$ in RA and 0.08 mas yr$^{-1}$ in Dec, corresponding to 1.8 km s$^{-1}$ and 3.2 km s$^{-1}$. The reference frame stability between IR and maser astrometry is 10~$μ$as yr$^{-1}$ (0.40 km s$^{-1}$) in RA and 15 $μ$as yr$^{-1}$ (0.57 km s$^{-1}$) in Dec. The masers show substantial variability in flux density and velocity structure, most notably IRS~7, which shows a 30-fold brightening in a blueshifted component since 2022. This variability may set a floor on future astrometry improvements and especially measurements of radial acceleration.

title: The SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper (LVM): Technical Overview
summary: The Sloan Digital Sky Survey V (SDSS-V) Local Volume Mapper (LVM) is an ultra-wide integral field spectroscopic survey of the Milky Way, the Magellanic Clouds, and a sample of galaxies in the local volume. The LVM spatially resolved spectroscopy covers the bulk of the optical range (3600-9800 A) at medium spectral-resolution (R = 2200-5500), and maps the disks of these galaxies at high physical spatial resolution (< 1 pc in the MW and ~10 pc in the Magellanic Clouds). Observations are carried out with the LVM Instrument (LVM-I), a custom-built robotic telescope, instrument, and facility located at Las Campanas Observatory (LCO) in Chile. In this article we present a technical overview of the LVM project. We describe the hardware, the survey observing strategy, and the details of how science and calibration observations are carried out. We provide a high-level overview of the survey data flow, including the reduction and calibration of the LVM spectra, and the production of the main data products that are released by the project. We also present an assessment of the LVM data quality and instrumental stability based on science observations. The main goal of this article is to serve as a primer for LVM users, providing the technical information required for the adequate analysis, modeling, and interpretation of the LVM data.

title: Shear viscosity from complex light-cone expansion
summary: Near thermal equilibrium, the transverse momentum density in a fluid diffuses according to $ω(k) \sim - i {\cal D} k^2$ at small $k$, where the diffusion coefficient ${\cal D}$ is proportional to the shear viscosity. In field theories with a holographic dual description in terms of classical gravity, the shear-mode frequency $ω(k)$ approaches the light cone at large imaginary wave vector. We develop a WKB approach to study this limit. For black branes in AdS$_{p+2}$, we determine the leading terms of the asymptotic large-$k$ expansion of the shear-mode frequency $ω(k)$. In the case of AdS$_{5}$, we compute a large number of terms of this series and use resummation techniques to analytically continue the result to small $k$. We find strong evidence that $ω(k)$ is analytic at $k=0$ and vanishes there, which amounts to the existence of hydrodynamics encoded in the large-$k$ physics. Taking 10 terms in the large-$k$ expansion of $ω(k)$ gives an answer for ${\cal D}$ which is accurate to better than $0.5\%$.

title: Gauge conditions in the perturbative quantization of quadratic gravity and its quantum Lagrangian
summary: In the perturbative formulation of the Hamiltonian of quadratic gravity, a specific gauge condition is required to hold the equivalence of the Hamiltonian equations of motion with the covariant field equations. Here we give robust evidence that this is an effect of perturbations, the exact nonperturbative equations of both formulations are equivalent, with no need of specific gauge conditions. Despite this, the required gauge condition must be imposed in the perturbative approach. We use it, together with other conditions obtained on very broad grounds, to obtain the quantum Lagrangian resulting from the integration on the canonical variables of the BFV quantization of the theory. This allow us to characterize the quantum modes from the Lagrangian perspective.

title: All Order Self-Dual Correlators From Symmetries
summary: We consider the scalar actions for self-dual Yang-Mills and self-dual gravity. We give a novel resummed version of their infinite tower of symmetries. We show that the Ward identities for symmetries corresponding to the individual levels of the infinite tower give the soft limits for wavefunction coefficients, while their resummed version completely fixes the full wavefunction. Our analysis is valid for general boundary conditions. Finally, we give an explicit formula for the $n$-point wavefunction coefficient as a single determinant reorganising the perturbiner solution, which also satisfies the soft limits.

title: Melonic ladder holography with a single free bulk field in AdS$_{d+1}$
summary: We derive a cylinder from the pair Casimir of a CFT$_d$: at zero centre momentum it depends only on relative dilations and rotations. Relative-coordinate radial quantisation then encodes exchanged family labels as cylinder energies. For a melonic CFT$_d$ in the normalisable and stable range, the reduced ladder sum is the Robin boundary-to-boundary propagator of a single free scalar field in rigid AdS$_{d+1}$, with the cylinder as its conformal boundary. The Robin boundary condition and bulk regularity (or parity) determine the holographic radial extension of the boundary data. A nonzero Robin boundary coefficient in global AdS breaks $2d$ AdS generators, yet the scalar's boundary propagator still encodes the conformal data of the melonic ladder. We demonstrate the correspondence for the Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev and the $d=2$ disorder-free long-range Amit--Roginsky melonic models, which correspond to a single free local scalar in AdS$_2$ and AdS$_3$, respectively.

title: All-multiplicity $\textrm{AdS}_4$ correlators in the self-dual sector
summary: It was recently shown that tree-level gluon correlators of any multiplicity in $\textrm{AdS}_4$ admit an expansion in terms of flat-space scattering amplitudes, where lower-point amplitudes in the expansion depend on merged external data. We derive here analogous formulae for correlators of scalar theories which encode the self-dual sectors of Yang-Mills theory and gravity in this background. In the latter case, the amplitudes are differential operators which can be obtained from the former using a simple double copy prescription in terms of kinematic numerators satisfying color-kinematics duality.

title: The Impact of Inclination, Redshift, and Mass Ratio Selection on Cosmological Constraints from Bright Sirens Beyond Conventional Fisher Approximations
summary: Future generations of gravitational-wave observatories are projected to detect up to thousands bright siren events within a decade of operation. However, the precision of these cosmological forecasts depends heavily on the astrophysical assumptions embedded within the simulation pipelines. In this work, we systematically investigate the impact of variations in the binary mass ratio ($q$), the maximum observable inclination angle ($ι_{\max}$), and the maximum redshift ($z_{\max}$) on the constraints of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and the matter density parameter ($Ω_m$). We perform our analyses based on the GWDALI framework, the GW Doublet Approximation, and the phenomenological waveform approximant IMRPhenomD. By adopting sets of non-spinning binary neutron star populations we explore the impact of astrophysical parameters on the constraints of cosmological parameters. Our results reveal a clear dichotomy in the observational requirements: while the statistical uncertainty on $H_0$ falls below the falls below approximately $1.3\%$ level for $N \ge 400$ events and drops under $0.9\%$ once $N \ge 800$, a deep-redshift catalog ($z_{\max} \ge 1.0$) is strictly required to effectively break parameter degeneracies and constrain the global geometry through $Ω_m$. Furthermore, expanding the maximum inclination cutoff from the conservative $20^{\circ}$ up to $40^{\circ}$ substantially mitigates the correlation between distance and inclination.

title: Exceptional points and hysteresis in Kerr-Newman quasi-normal modes
summary: Exceptional points (EPs) and eigenstate hysteresis, previously found in Kerr only with an auxiliary scalar field, arise intrinsically in the quasinormal-mode spectrum of Kerr-Newman black holes. Using a hyperboloidal formulation of the coupled gravito-electromagnetic Teukolsky equations and a Chebyshev pseudospectral method, we compute the $\ell=m=2$ spectrum and locate four EPs at up to $99.974\%$ of extremality, one from a new repulsion. The gaps close as a square root branch point, and quasistatic loops around one or more EPs exchange the coalescing modes, confirming hysteresis.

title: Can Spontaneous Time-Translation Symmetry Breaking Be Quantized Without Explicit Branches?
comment: The manuscript has 16 pages, 3 figures, and 1 table
summary: Can classically branched dynamics associated with spontaneous time-translation-symmetry breaking be quantized without explicitly retaining the branches of the Hamiltonian? We investigate this question using a reduced phase space. formulation in which the Hamiltonian is single-valued, while the critical structure of the classical Legendre map is encoded in a singular, momentum-dependent symplectic geometry. Quantization of the reduced Poisson algebra yields a deformed position-momentum commutator whose singularities determine distinct regular momentum sectors. Using the positive measure induced by the reduced symplectic structure, we identify a bounded central sector and two unbounded outer sectors. In the central sector, states with vanishing mean momentum obey a nonzero lower bound on position uncertainty, subject to the operator-domain assumptions of the representation. We further identify a possible field-theoretic connection with k-essence, where nonlinear scalar-field kinetics can produce finite-velocity degeneracies of the Legendre map. The relationship between the resulting reduced quantum description and branch-matching quantization remains unresolved and requires a comparison of the corresponding Hilbert spaces and operator domains.

title: Horizon entropy does not by itself determine a force between black holes
comment: 26 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Companion paper: "A Relabeling Obstruction to Transporting Horizon Entropy". Code and data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23442562
summary: The Bekenstein-Hawking law fixes the total entropy of a horizon. Membrane, holographic, and entropic-force pictures go further and follow the entropy of individual horizon elements as a configuration changes. We show that this step needs structure that the horizon geometry does not supply. Along a family of horizons labeled by $λ$, a relabeling of horizon points by a tangential field $v^A$ shifts the temperature-weighted entropy variation $\int T\partial_λ(dS)$ exactly by $-\int v^AD_AT dS$, so the horizon data determine it only when the temperature is uniform. We test this on two black holes in exact Brill-Lindquist data. At fixed physical masses each horizon area is independent of the separation through five relative orders; the low-order equilibrium force reported earlier comes from holding the bare parameters fixed instead. Weighting the redistribution of area by the nonuniform Noether-charge temperature gives a candidate repulsion equal to $(ν/8)(GM/r_{12})^3$ times the Newtonian attraction, for total mass $M$, symmetric mass ratio $ν$, and coordinate separation $r_{12}$. As a static interaction it would shift the third post-Newtonian coefficient of the circular-orbit binding energy by $5ν/48$, in conflict with general relativity. The identity resolves the conflict. Through fourth post-Newtonian order the candidate lies entirely in the dipole of the area distribution, which the uniform part of the companion's field generates as a Möbius map of the labels, and which vanishes in the area-balanced conformal frame, where the functional begins at fifth order with a coefficient that a further relabeling can still change. The marginally trapped tube of the data and the tidally deformed horizon of a post-Newtonian binary, both of which do supply an identification, transport no dipole at the order the candidate requires.

title: Gauge-field energy density in inflationary kinetic-coupling models: QFT regularization versus horizon cutoffs
summary: Coupling gauge fields to the inflaton can amplify their quantum fluctuations during inflation, with potential applications to a range of cosmological phenomena. A central challenge is to define finite and physically meaningful observables, such as the gauge-field energy density. In this work, we study an Abelian gauge field kinetically coupled to the inflaton through $f^2(φ)F_{μν}F^{μν}$ in a de Sitter background with $f\propto a^{γ_1}$, and compare conventional quantum-field-theoretic regularization with horizon-cutoff prescriptions. Using a hard physical-momentum cutoff and dimensional regularization, we derive the ultraviolet divergences in closed form and fix the remaining one-parameter finite-part ambiguity by requiring the coupling-induced total energy density to be nonnegative. We then examine five horizon-cutoff prescriptions based on characteristic scales of the mode equations. Their predictions depend sensitively on the choice of horizon scale and, for weak gauge-field production, can deviate substantially from the regularized result; for the adopted finite-part prescription, the minimal horizon agrees best with the regularized total energy density. As $|γ_1|\to 2$, where infrared modes dominate, the relative deviation of all prescriptions from the regularized result vanishes, independently of the finite-part prescription. Outside this regime, the separate electric and magnetic contributions, which can become negative after regularization, are not reliably reproduced by any of the horizon-cutoff prescriptions.

title: In situ enhanced detectability of axions' responses in a microwave cavity
summary: Microwave cavities in strong magnetic fields are among the most sensitive detectors for axion dark matter detection. Its sensitivity, however, is fundamentally limited by the second order nature of axion photon energy conversion, which yields an extremely weak signal. Here we propose a feasible approach to break this limitation, by pre-exciting the target cavity mode to generate a first order power response signal in situ. The resulting signal amplitude scales linearly with the axion-photon coupling parameter, which is in sharp contrast to the quadratic scaling of conventional schemes, and is detectable via standard quadrature balanced homodyne detection system, even though its phase remains stochastic. Numerical simulations demonstrate that this pre-excited seed field can effectively suppress thermal noise, and thus the detection sensitivity of the system can approach the lower quantum noise limit. Consequently, the sensitivities predicted by the KSVZ and DFSZ models could be surpassed. This proposal might offer a pathway to a major leap in axion dark matter searches, as it is within reach of current technology.

title: Joint Angular-Power Distributions of Interfering Nanohertz Gravitational Waves
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures; 7 pages of Supplemental Material with 1 figure
summary: Finite populations of supermassive black-hole binaries produce fluctuations in both gravitational-wave power and pulsar timing correlations. We characterize the realization-dependent, orientation-averaged Earth-term angular correlation through its frequency-resolved Legendre coefficients. A hybrid model of bright sources and a Gaussian faint background extends the conditional Gamma distribution in the many-weak-source limit to non-central $χ^2$ statistics, yielding correlated multipoles after population marginalization. Our analytical variance decomposition and SMBHB population simulations reveal a population-dependent transition from interference dominated variance at low frequencies to population-power-dominated variance at high frequencies. In the many-weak-source regime, a multivariate lognormal approximation captures the main features of the joint distribution using only the first two log-cumulants. These results provide statistical benchmarks for fluctuations in both the overall amplitude and angular structure of the realized correlation.

title: FeynFacet: AI agents for analytic NLO QCD
summary: We present FeynFacet, a workflow in which artificial intelligence agents develop and execute programs for analytic next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD calculations, with the observables and conventions specified by physicists. We use it to derive new analytic hard functions for single-inclusive transverse spin transfer in proton-proton and lepton-proton collisions. The new proton-proton results cover all partonic channels contributing to transverse spin transfer, and the new lepton-proton result is inclusive in the scattered lepton. Within FeynFacet, we use reverse unitarity to represent the on-shell delta functions in real-emission phase-space integrals as cut propagators. Dimensional shifts convert integrals containing evanescent numerators into scalar integrals in higher dimensions. Integration-by-parts identities then reduce the scalar integrals to master integrals, which are evaluated analytically. Gauge invariance, pole cancellation and renormalization-group (RG) evolution provide checks throughout the calculation. We reproduce established single-inclusive hard functions for unpolarized and double longitudinally polarized proton-proton and lepton-proton scattering, and for proton-proton scattering with two transversely polarized beams. We also reproduce the NLO matching coefficients for unpolarized quark and gluon transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions and the associated soft functions. The new transverse spin-transfer coefficients provide perturbative inputs for extracting quark transversity through spin-dependent fragmentation, including polarized-hyperon production, Collins and dihadron asymmetries in jets, and spin-dependent one- and two-point energy correlators. We make all analytic coefficients and the associated calculation programs publicly available online.

title: Soft scalar-field corrections to the topological susceptibility
summary: We compute the contribution from soft scalar-field fluctuations to the topological susceptibility in SU(2) gauge theory at high temperature. We construct a 3-dimensional effective theory for the scalar field that accounts for the presence of an instanton. In the limit that the scalar selfcoupling $ λ$ is much larger than the square of the gauge coupling $g$ we obtain a correction of order $\sqrtλ$ relative to the 1-loop result for the topological susceptibility.

title: Prospects of Detecting Cosmological Domain Walls in the Cosmic Microwave Background
summary: Topological defects are a generic prediction of field theories with spontaneously broken symmetries, and domain walls, the two-dimensional defects left by a broken discrete symmetry, are among the simplest. We study the imprint of dark, purely gravitationally interacting domain walls on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), in the regime where a low symmetry-breaking scale $η$ allows the walls to evade the Zel'dovich overclosure bound while remaining cosmologically relevant. The relativistic repulsion of matter by a planar wall carves out an evacuated void bounded by an overdense shell, and we compute the resulting photon deflection field analytically for walls both aligned with and arbitrarily inclined to the line of sight. The deflection stamps coherent, strongly non-Gaussian distortions onto the temperature sky, with a characteristic two-peak structure set by the relativistic displacement scale and an inclination dependence that vanishes for face-on walls. Because these signatures are localised and anisotropic, they are poorly captured by two-point statistics; we therefore analyse them with a curvelet/wavelet decomposition matched to the wall's geometry, and with simulation-based inference, training a Neural Posterior Estimator (NPE) to recover the scattering redshift $z$, energy scale $η$, and inclination $θ$, and a Neural Ratio Estimator (NRE) to evaluate the likelihood-ratio test statistic for limit-setting. Casting these methods as sensitivity forecasts for a South Pole Telescope-like (SPT) survey, we find that the curvelet and wavelet statistical thresholds populate a common $η\sim 10-100$ MeV band over the accessible redshift range. The neural-ratio sensitivity curve, which exploits the full map morphology, reaches a factor 1.3-1.9 lower in $η$ at $z \gtrsim 20$, or $\sim 2-7$ in the wall tension, landing essentially on the per-resolution-element noise floor.

title: Minkowski metric signature as a statistical prediction of piecewise-flat quantum gravity
summary: We study an ab initio calculation of the signature of the spacetime metric, within the framework of piecewise-flat models of quantum gravity. Applying numerical techniques, we evaluate the probability that any 4-simplex in a triangulation of a spacetime manifold has a given metric signature. For this we use a toy-model of quantum gravity based on quantum Regge calculus, where we ignore any effects due to dynamics and focus only on the kinematics of the configuration space. Our results may hold even for other QG models, as long as they behave similarly in the same approximation. We obtain that for a suitably chosen spacelike domain of edge lengths and the UV cutoff, the probability of observing Minkowski signature reaches approximately 85%. In contrast, allowing both spacelike and timelike edge lengths leads to the split signature being dominant, with probability between 72% and 81%. The results are essentially independent of the choice of topology and triangulation of the spacetime manifold. Our findings demonstrate that the signature of the metric does not necessarily need to be postulated in a given model of quantum gravity, but can instead be predicted from it, and we estimate the relative size of the UV cutoff and the domain for edge lengths that a given model should incorporate in order to predict the Minkowski signature with high probability. There is a potential to further increase this probability by taking into account the dynamics of the theory.

title: Equation of state of hot and dense QCD using the complex Langevin equation
summary: We present continuum-extrapolated lattice results for the QCD equation of state at high temperatures and unprecedentedly large baryon chemical potentials. These results were obtained by performing the first complex Langevin simulations at the physical value of the pion mass. We work in a strangeness-neutral, charm-neutral, and isospin-symmetric setup and show results for the baryon density, pressure, and trace anomaly as a function of baryon chemical potential and temperature, respectively.

title: Analytic two-loop corrections to top-quark pair production at hadron colliders
comment: comments: 35 pages (main) + 10 pages (appendices), 7 figures; analytic results at https://zenodo.org/records/23469687; numerical code at https://gitlab.com/hqpamp/hqpamp
summary: We present the complete two-loop QCD amplitudes for the production of a top-quark pair in the quark--antiquark annihilation and gluon-fusion channels in analytic form up to order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$. Our analysis maintains full dependence on the top-quark mass and on the number of colours. The amplitudes are expressed in terms of 417 master integrals, which we compute by means of differential equations in $\varepsilon$-factorised form. Their calculation involves several elliptic curves and a hyperelliptic curve of genus two, which makes top-quark pair production an ideal arena for recent methods to construct canonical bases beyond polylogarithms. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first scattering amplitude in which iterated integrals related to a genus-two surface survive in the finite remainder in four space-time dimensions. We provide high-precision series expansions at the threshold and combine them with the numerical solution of the differential equations in a code that evaluates the UV-renormalised infrared-finite remainders at arbitrary points of the physical phase space.

title: Stochastic dynamics of cosmological inflation in general relativity
summary: The theory of Inflation, supplemented by fluctuations of the quantum vacuum, is the leading paradigm to explain the correlations of inhomogeneities at very large distances in the Universe. Particle physics methods fail when strong non-linearity and non-perturbativity are involved, leaving a whole landscape of untestable scenarios of inflation. Starobinsky's stochastic inflation can in principle treat inflationary inhomogeneities nonlinearly and classically as the Hubble radius becomes smaller than their wavelengths, but it was never formulated in full general relativity, which motivates this thesis. Using the Keldysh formalism of nonequilibrium quantum field theory, we first develop a validity criterion for the use of classical computations, and thus simulations, to probe inflationary interactions, finding analytically that the bispectrum can be extracted from slightly sub-Hubble scales in quasi-de Sitter spacetimes. We then provide the first analytical solutions to the constraints for inhomogeneous initial conditions of numerical relativity simulations of inflation, and use them to explore its nonperturbative regime. Our main contribution is to obtain stochastic equations for the full set of inflaton equations in general relativity: this description incorporates the full nonlinear and backreacting evolution, is small-gauge-invariant, and is free of historical assumptions such as the gradient-free separate universe approximation. We implement these equations in the BSSN formulation of numerical relativity, demonstrating their correctness in slow-roll and ultra slow-roll scenarios via the satisfaction of the constraints, with a first look at eternal inflation. Finally, we extend our coarse-graining methods beyond General Relativity and single-field inflation, offering a phenomenological framework with the ambition of serving as a numerical particle collider for the early universe.

title: Entanglement entropy of evolving wormholes
summary: We compute the entanglement entropy of a discretized scalar field in the fixed spacetime background of an evolving wormhole. Evolving wormholes are a class of time dependent and spherically symmetric wormhole geometries. In both expanding and contracting models, we find dynamically generated entanglement. Asymptotically far from the wormhole throat, the entanglement entropy is well described by the leading term in the area law, although its coefficient can depend sensitively on the value of the UV cutoff. As the UV cutoff is decreased, the coefficient becomes progressively less sensitive to the cutoff, providing numerical evidence that it approaches a cutoff-independent value in the continuum limit. Near the throat, we find a double-dip structure in the entanglement entropy which cannot be described by the leading and logarithmic contributions to the area law.

title: First-Order Structure of the Linearised Einstein Equations: Constant-Curvature Backgrounds
summary: Teukolsky's decoupled equations and Wald's adjoint method of metric reconstruction are built from second-order operators: the linearised Einstein operator G, the curvature-extraction operator T, the decoupled operator O and the reconstruction operator S^*, related by SG=OT. We show that on four-dimensional constant-curvature backgrounds with non-zero Lambda all of these operators factor into first-order maps through a single intermediate variable: the perturbation of the self-dual half of the spin connection. We also show that for non-zero Lambda the metric perturbation is itself obtained from the connection perturbation by a first-order map. The connection therefore gives a complete description of linearised gravity, and the fourth-order identity SG=OT follows by composition from a single second-order identity. Using conformal flatness, we choose the Hertz-potential map so that, after a conformal rescaling, the potential obeys the flat wave equation component by component. This leads to a new reconstruction scheme, in which the potential is sourced by the curvature psi, which in turn obeys a decoupled sourced equation. A prescribed curvature is then reached by a second-order rather than a fourth-order equation, and the corrector is local and algebraic in the stress-energy tensor. The price is that the full curvature, rather than a single component, must be determined, and that the reality of the reconstructed metric becomes a condition, which we argue holds for retarded solutions. We illustrate the scheme for a static point mass in de Sitter space, where it gives a real metric perturbation that agrees with linearised Schwarzschild-de Sitter up to a diffeomorphism. We view these results as a proof of concept for a first-order Teukolsky-Wald framework on Kerr.
